headline: Nine killed in road accidents across four districts, 52 injured
summary: At least nine people died and 52 were injured in a series of road accidents across Jamalpur, Chattogram, Mymensingh, and Lalmonirhat yesterday. The incidents involved trucks, motorcycles, easy-bikes, and a bus.
details: At least nine people were killed and 52 others injured in separate road accidents across Jamalpur, Chattogram, Mymensingh, and Lalmonirhat yesterday. These incidents involved various vehicles including trucks, motorcycles, easy-bikes, and a bus.

In Jamalpur's Melandah upazila, four people, including three family members (Morshed Alam, Ikrama, and their eight-month-old daughter Rifa), died when a truck hit a motorcycle and then an easy-bike. The motorcycle rider, Shawkat Hasan Likhan, 45, also perished in the collision.

Chattogram's Satkania upazila saw two fatalities and 40 injuries when a bus carrying teachers, students, and guardians on a study tour plunged into a roadside ditch. The deceased were identified as teacher Sohana Afroz, 45, and Md Israfil, 56, husband of another teacher.

Mymensingh's Nandail upazila reported two unidentified men, aged 28-32, killed and five injured in a head-on collision between a dump truck and a pickup van. Separately, in Lalmonirhat's Aditmari upazila, an 11-year-old madrasa student, Habibur Rahman, died and four others were injured after a truck collided with a battery-run auto-rickshaw.
caption:

Chattogram's Satkania upazila saw two fatalities and 40 injuries when a bus carrying teachers, students, and guardians on a study tour plunged into a roadside ditch. The deceased were identified as teacher Sohana Afroz, 45, and Md Israfil, 56, husband of another teacher.

Mymensingh's Nandail upazila reported two unidentified men, aged 28-32, killed and five injured in a head-on collision between a dump truck and a pickup van. headline: Three more die of dengue, 1,674 hospitalised in 24 hours across Bangladesh
summary: The latest figures from the DGHS show a concerning rise in dengue cases and fatalities. This brings the total death toll to 458 and cumulative cases to 1,47,580 this year.
details: At least three dengue patients died and 1,674 others were hospitalised in the 24 hours till 8:00am yesterday, according to the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS).
Of the reported deaths, two occurred in Dhaka division and one in Barishal division, highlighting the widespread impact of the disease.
With these latest fatalities, the total death toll from dengue has now risen to 458. The cumulative number of dengue cases recorded this year has reached 1,47,580.
Currently, 5,826 dengue patients are undergoing treatment at various hospitals across the country, indicating a significant burden on the healthcare system.
caption:
Bangladesh reports 3 more dengue deaths and 1,674 new hospitalisations in the last 24 hours. The total death toll for the year now stands at 458.

At least three dengue patients died and 1,674 others were hospitalised in the 24 hours till 8:00am yesterday, according to the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS).

Of the reported deaths, two occurred in Dhaka division and one in Barishal division, highlighting the widespread impact of the disease.

With these latest fatalities, the total death toll from dengue has now risen to 458. The cumulative number of dengue cases recorded this year has reached 1,47,580.

Currently, 5,826 dengue patients are undergoing treatment at various hospitals across the country, indicating a significant burden on the healthcare system.
